reasons: The tile format must match the server, and no check of that match is visible.
Error handling is left to the components that call these hooks.

terms.meaning: A written description of the shape of data a value should have.
A web address on the server that returns data when asked.
A stored copy of data kept so it does not need to be requested again.
Asking the server for fresh data at a fixed interval.
Packing three facts (category, state and used flag) into one letter for each datapoint.

sections.name: File setup, Phase, CollationTool, CollationStage
sections.title: Shared names and stage shape
sections.what: Defines the five phase names, the two tool names and what one stage of a run contains, such as its label, status, start and finish times and note.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives every file the same vocabulary for runs and stages.
sections.watch_out: Adding or renaming a phase here also means updating the drawing engine's phase list.

sections.name: CollationModel, CollationDemo
sections.title: Run record and demo list shapes
sections.what: Describes everything in a run record: title, status, timestamps, stages, groups, projects with their tile codes, slides and counts. It also describes the demo list.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the field names, which presumably match the server's response.
sections.watch_out: Field names must match the server exactly. A renamed field breaks the view without a clear message.

sections.name: decodeTile, TERMINAL_RUN
sections.title: Tile decoder and finished statuses
sections.what: Turns one tile letter into a category (cost, schedule, capacity or other), a state (none, sourced, verified or flagged) and a used flag. It also lists the statuses that mean a run has ended.
sections.why: Likely reason: packing three facts into one character keeps large runs small to send.
sections.watch_out: Tile letters are read by their character code, so any change in the server's encoding breaks the colours silently.

sections.name: useCollation
sections.title: Live run data loader
sections.what: Requests a run record and asks again every 3 seconds while the run is live and not finished. Once finished, the record is kept and not refreshed.
sections.why: Likely reason: a live run keeps changing, while a finished run does not, so polling stops when the run ends.
sections.watch_out: Polling stops only when the status is one of the finished values, so an unexpected status would keep polling indefinitely.

sections.name: useCollationDemo
sections.title: Demo list loader
sections.what: Requests the pinned demo runs when enabled and keeps the answer for five minutes.
sections.why: Likely reason: the demo list rarely changes, so repeated requests are avoided.
sections.watch_out: The request runs only when the enabled flag is set, so callers must pass that flag correctly.

summary: Defines the data shapes for a collation run and the functions that load run data and demo runs from the server.
purpose: Gives the front end one shared description of run records, the tile code format, and the requests that fetch them.
why: Likely reason: keeps the request and data definitions in one place so the view and the drawing engine agree on what they receive.
how: 1. Defines the types for stages, the run record and the demo list. 2. Decodes each tile letter into a category, a state and a used flag. 3. Lists the statuses that mean a run has finished. 4. Loads run data and refreshes every 3 seconds while the run is live and unfinished. 5. Loads the demo list and keeps it for 5 minutes.
inputs: A tool name, a run identifier, a live flag and an enabled flag for the demo request.
outputs: Typed data shapes, a decoded tile value, and two data-loading hooks that report loading, error and data states.
risks: The tile letters must match what the server writes. A mismatch shows wrong colours without any error.
debug: If colours look wrong, check the tile decoding first. If data never refreshes, check the status values and the live flag. If the demo list is missing, check the endpoint and the enabled flag.
